title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: SailPoint Identity Security Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Covers SailPoint Identity Security Cloud (SailPoint Human Fabric). SaaS tenant (docs now branded SailPoint Human Fabric); VA is customer-hosted; no plan gating found for these token controls.

controls.name: Delete personal access token
controls.what: Owner deletes a PAT from Preferences; admins can delete via DELETE /personal-access-tokens/{id}.
controls.setting: Preferences > Personal Access Tokens > Delete; DELETE /personal-access-tokens/{id}

controls.name: Org Admin Personal Access Tokens page
controls.what: Org Admins view all non-managed PATs with owner, scopes, expiry and last used, and can update expiry.
controls.setting: Admin > Global > Security Settings > Personal Access Tokens

controls.name: PAT expiration date
controls.what: Set or update PAT expiry; default 6 months, blank means never expires.
controls.setting: PAT form expiration date; expirationDate / userAwareTokenNeverExpires in API

controls.name: accessTokenValiditySeconds
controls.what: Sets how long each issued bearer token lives (PAT default 43200s).

controls.name: Scopes
controls.what: Select scopes to narrow access below the user level; UI default is a no-authorization scope, API default is sp:scopes:all.
controls.setting: Scopes checkboxes on PAT / API client forms

controls.name: Support/Services PAT auto-deletion
controls.what: PATs created by SailPoint Support/Services accounts are deleted when tenant access expires.

no_control.what: No setting to stop users from creating PATs; docs say any user can create one (limited to the user's own user levels and 10 tokens per user).

controls_unknown: Any org setting to disable PAT creation or require approval for PATs/API clients
Any admin-enforced maximum PAT lifetime (API states no upper limit on expirationDate but the doc only says this, not that no policy exists)
Whether Network Settings IP/geo restrictions apply to /oauth/token or API calls
Whether deleting a PAT or API client invalidates already-issued bearer tokens (scope changes do not affect existing bearer tokens)
Audit event names for PAT/API client create, use, delete (published sample list is partial and lists none)
Whether API read calls (search, list identities) produce audit events
Whether disabling the owning identity stops its PATs
VA key lifetime, rotation and use logging

authentication.summary: A PAT is a client ID and secret tied to a user. The holder posts them to /oauth/token (client credentials) and gets a JWT bearer token that acts with the owner's user level, narrowed by scopes.

federation.details: Docs do not state whether PAT use is subject to the IdP. The token exchange is non-interactive, so IdP conditional access is not consulted at use time per the flow description.

ip_restriction.boundary: PAT API calls follow the owner's identity-profile Network Settings (CIDR network, country allow/block list) when Off Network / Untrusted Geographies is set on that profile. Stated in the Non-Employee Risk Management docs for PATs generated in Identity Security. The tenant docs say these restrictions are skipped for SSO users; whether that exception affects PAT calls is not stated.

lifetime.summary: PAT: 6 months default, can be never-expiring; bearer token 43200s default

renewal.expiry_basis: PAT expirationDate; each bearer token expires per accessTokenValiditySeconds
renewal.summary: Holder re-exchanges the PAT secret for new bearer tokens until the PAT expires or is deleted. Expired PATs can be restored for 3 months.

administration.summary: Any user can create up to 10 PATs. Org Admins can list, create and change expiry of non-managed PATs; managed (e.g. Workflows) PATs are hidden from the UI but listable via API.
administration.conditions: Org Admin for org-wide view; idn:all-personal-access-tokens:read for API listing

inventory.details: Org admins see non-managed PATs on Admin > Global > Security Settings > Personal Access Tokens; GET /personal-access-tokens without owner-id returns all tenant PATs (needs idn:all-personal-access-tokens:read). Managed PATs are not on the UI page.

network.ui: Admin > Global > System Settings > Network Settings (Network Definition / Trusted Countries); then Admin > Identity Management > Identity Profiles > profile > Block Access From: Off Network / Untrusted Geographies

token_format.notes: Bearer token is a JWT; PAT id is a client ID used as username for Basic Auth.

log_sources.name: Search > Events (events index, POST /search)
log_sources.notes: Kept one year plus current month; older up to 5 years via support request.

anomaly_cues: PATs or clients with sp:scopes:all or no expiry
lastUsed on stale tokens (updated once a day)

containment.steps: Delete the PAT (owner UI or DELETE /personal-access-tokens/{id}).
containment.notes: Docs say scope changes don't affect existing bearer tokens; deletion effect on live bearer tokens (default 12h) not documented.
